commands.checks: Standard library, about 3 s and under 30 MB, no file read or written. The exact solver finds the plain third call for each of the 32 calls that raise the plain middle term to level 3 and refuses a target two calls away; exact rational arithmetic and arithmetic modulo 2^61 - 1 give the same answers on 92 seeded cases; three wrong variants of the kind A rule are each rejected on 22 seeded cases; with coefficient -1 no same-frame part is finishable on 24 seeded cases. Prints PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_CONTROLS.

About 38 s and under 30 MB. Frame game at 3 address bits: 10,752 free elements, 56 paid calls; 32 of them raise the plain middle term to level 3; 4 undo the shared call and 48 could be the other array's last call. For both kinds of two-term part with coefficient 1 and every free element (reduced to 1,632 classes by the 8 free elements that commute with both calls): kind A 9,983 tested, 769 plain in disguise, 128 finishable by the call alone, 639 removable by a call that could be a last call, 1,407 removable by any call that does not undo the shared call; kind B 9,984, 768, 0, 128, 128; no case is both. The kind A rule matches every tested case: same frame with g of odd order finishable, same frame with g of even order removable (by all 52 calls tried), adjacent frames removable only by the 4 calls that cannot be a last call, further apart neither. The 128 removable kind B parts, and the 768 adjacent-frame kind A parts, are exactly the parts for which some call exchanges the frames of the two terms. The reduction to classes is tested directly on 80 cases that were not representatives. Prints PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_MAIN.

About 4 s. Kind A parts with frames further apart that are finished by one call followed by a free step on its output: a call t that raises the plain term M to level 3 with t.E = h.t.M, h free and 1 + c.h invertible; the identity (1 + c.h)^-1.(t.y) = t.M is checked term by term in exact arithmetic. 128 parts for c = 1 (h of order 3), 0 for c = -1, 512 for c = 2 and 512 for c = 1/2; by the rule checked in the other parts none of them is finishable by the call alone or removable. Whether this list is complete is not checked here. Prints PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_POSTSTEP.

About 42 s. The free elements carry the first call to each of the 56 paid calls; 48 shared calls give a level-2 term and the 768 symmetries of the question carry one of them to each of the others; the whole table is recomputed for a second shared call (w = 10) with the same counts and the same rule; the symmetry map is tested case by case on 368 distinct cases, with a symmetry that does not commute with the first call, among them all 128 removable kind B parts. Prints PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_SYMMETRY.

About 85 s. All tested cases for five more rows. Kind A with coefficient -1: none finishable by the call alone, 767 removable by a call that could be a last call, 1,535 by any call that does not undo the shared call. Kind A with 2 and with 1/2: the 767 same-frame cases finishable, none removable. The kind A rule with a coefficient matches every case. Kind B with -1: none finishable, the same 128 parts removable as with coefficient 1. Kind B with 2: none either way. None is both in any row. Prints PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_COEFFICIENTS.

About 22 s. One spare address bit (4 address bits, 240 paid calls): a seeded sample of 100 kind A parts with coefficient 1 (20 same frame with g of even order, 20 adjacent frames, 20 same frame with g of odd order, 40 further apart); the rule found at 3 address bits is right on every sampled case and none is both. A sample, not a complete table. Prints PASS_COMPLEX_M3_SHARED_CALL_SPARE.
